THIS FIRST APPEAL FROM ORDERS HAVING BEEN FINALLY ON 21.08.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

 Dated this the 21st day of August, 2024  JUDGMENT
The appeal is filed against the order dated 04.04.2024 in I.A.No.1 of 2023 in O.S.No.64 of 2023 of the Sub Court, Perumbavoor.
The suit is filed under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

Along with the suit, the plaintiffs have filed an application for temporary injunction restraining the 2 nd appellant herein from acting as President of the 1 st appellant Trust and presiding over the meeting of the Board of Directors, Executive Committee or Board of Trustees, till the disposal of the suit.
2. According to the plaintiffs, they are life Trustees of the 1st appellant Trust namely, Sree Narayana Gurukulam Charitable Trust established in the year 2001.
They 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 contended that the Trust is a public Trust represented by its Secretary as per the bye-law.
The bye-law provides for three types of Trustees namely, the Life Trustee, the Individual Trustee and the institution Trustee.

The relevant clause in the bye-laws dealing with the Board of Trustees, reads as follows:

sentences.text: "6. BOARD OF TRUSTEES
The overall administration, management and control of the affairs of the Trust and its properties shall vest in a Board of Trustees.

There shall be constituted in the following manner:
1* LIFE TRUSTEE
An individual who contributes or a Corporate body which contributes Rs.5 lakhs (Rupees five lakhs) shall be a LIFE TRUSTEE and such Trustees shall be the Members of the Board of Directors.
The Corporate Body will be represented by its President or by its Chief Executive.
(as amended on 14.11.2004)
2. INDIVIDUAL TRUSTEE
An Individual who contributes or a Corporate Body 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 which contributes Rs. 1 lakh shall be an Individual Trustee.
The Corporate Body shall be represented by its President or by its Chief Executive.
3. INSTITUTIONAL TRUSTEE
An individual who contributes or a Corporate Body which contributes Rs.25000 shall be an institutional trustee.
The representative of the Corporate Body shall be its President or its Chief Executive.
One fourth of the Institutional Trustees shall be represented in the Board of Trustees.
The Trustee shall be a member of S.N.D.P. Yogam.
In the event of death or insolvency of a Trustee his legal heir shall be nominated as the Trustee.
Among the successors only one person will be entitled, with the approval of the Board of Directors, to be a Trustee.
The application for Trusteeship shall be in the form as shown in the Annexure."
3. As per clause 9(a) dealing with Executive Committee it is stated that the Committee shall consist of 11 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 members viz. President, Vice President, Secretary,
Joint Secretary, Treasurer and six committee members

. It is stated that the President of the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union shall be the ex-officio President of the Committee and the Vice President, Secretary, Joint Secretary, Treasurer and six committee members are to be elected from among the Board of Directors.

As per Clause 11, the President is to preside over the meetings of the Board of Directors, Executive Committee and the Board of Directors and regarding matters on which there is a difference of opinion, it shall be decided by majority votes and the President shall have a second or a casting vote in case of a tie.
Clause 11 further says that in the absence of the President, the Vice President shall exercise all powers vested with the President.
4. The Kunnathunadu SNDP Union has superseded by the SNDP Yogam by exercising the power available under Clause 28 of the Rules governing the Yogam.

2024 :KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 Clause 28 empowers the Yogam to stop the functioning of a Union or to cancel the appointment of any officers or committee members of the Union and to conduct fresh election for filling up such vacancies and to appoint necessary officers in the interregnum for managing the affairs of the temple, bhajanamadam, school etc.
After superseding the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union, The General Secretary of the Yogam has appointed an Executive Committee for managing the affairs of the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union.

sentences.text: 3 Chairman of the Administrative Committee so appointed.
In his capacity as the Chairman of the Administrative Committee, the 2nd appellant contends that he is entitled to preside over the meetings of the 1 st appellant Trust.

The counsel for the appellants says that the Administrative Committee and its Chairman are only successors-in-interest of the Board of Management of the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 and being successors-in-interest the 2nd appellant is entitled to do all functions that the President of the Union is entitled to.

entities.text: Board of Management of the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union 2024
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is hence contended that since one of the powers of the President is to be the ex-officio President of the 1st appellant Trust, there can be no objection to the 2nd appellant presiding over the meetings of the Trust.
In essence this is the contention on which the injunction application is sought to be defended.
5. The trial court rejected the contentions of the appellants and granted an order of injunction.
The court specifically found that as per Ext.A1, the administration of the Trust is vested with the Executive Committee having 11 members.
It is noted that the President is ex-officio and not a person elected from the Board of Directors.

It is further noted as per Ext.A1 that, Kunnathunadu SNDP Union shall have a Committee comprising of the Union President, Union Vice President, Union Secretary and representatives from SNDP 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 yogam Director Board and members from Union Panchayat and members of the Saka Yogam as per Rule 10.
Rule 11 says that the Union committee members will be elected in the Annual General Body with a tenure of three years.
The President of the Union is an elected President.

The trial court found that as at present there is no elected President for the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union and there is no provision which warrants the Chairman of the Administrative Committee to be the ex-officio President of the 1st appellant Trust.

The court found that there is no provision in Ext.A2 to consider such a Chairman as the President of the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union and hence the Chairman of the Administrative Committee appointed through Exts.A3 and A4 orders, cannot be considered as a President as provided under the bye-law.
It is on the above reasoning that the injunction application has been allowed.

The counsel for the appellants relied on the decision of a Division Bench of this Court in Manager,
St.Mary's H.S. v. Beji Abraham [2002 KHC 88] to submit that the de facto doctrine saves those acts de facto performed by officers within the scope of their assumed official authority.

Manager,
St.Mary's H.S. v. Beji Abraham [2002 KHC 88]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said decision has no bearing on the facts of this case.
This is not a case where any action taken by a person, who has wrongly assumed office needs to be saved, by resorting to the de facto doctrine.
This is a case where a person who has wrongly assumed office is sought to be dislodged from the office.

Reliance is also placed on the judgment of the High Court of Bombay in Rehman and Ors. Vs. The Corporation of the City of Nagpur and Ors.[AIR 1970 Bom 394] and the judgment of Madras High Court in In Re: Palanisamy Chettiar [AIR 1957 Mad 351].

entities.text: Rehman and Ors. Vs. The Corporation of the City of Nagpur and Ors.[AIR 1970 Bom 394]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Rehman and Ors.(supra) the question involved was whether the Administrator appointed on supersession of the Nagpur Corporation can be 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 treated as the "local authority" under Section 2(viii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The High Court after considering the statutory provisions held that the Administrator would be the successor to the superseded Corporation.

The court relied on the provisions contained in Section 409(2) of the City of Nagpur Corporation Act,

sentences.text: The said judgment rendered on the basis of statutory provisions, cannot have any application to a case where there is no backing of any governing statutory provision.
In Palanisamy Chettiar (Supra) the Madras High Court was considering the appointment of District Magistrates as Assistant Sessions Judges.
The court found that there is nothing violative in appointing District Magistrates generally by virtue of their office as Assistant Sessions Judges.
The said judgment again does not deal with the issue involved in this 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 case.
In the case on hand, as per the bye-laws, the President of the Kunnathunadu SNDP Union is to be the ex-officio President of the Committee.
The persona is specified in the Trust deed there is no provision either in the Trust deed or in bye-laws of the Union regarding the replacement of the President by any other person.

The Chairman of the Executive Committee cannot be treated as a successor-in-interest of the President but the Executive Committee itself can only be treated as a body which has been authorised to carry out the functions of the Union in the event of the supersession.
Such an eventuality is not considered in the Trust deed which governs the 1st appellant Trust.
At the same time, the Trust deed specifically says that in the absence of the President, the Vice President will carry out the functions of the Trust.
As such, it is not a case where there is any vacancy in the office.

The Trust deed contemplates the situation where there can be a stage where the President is not available and the Vice 2024:KER:64053 FAO NO. 55 OF 2024 President will have to take over all the functions.
The 1 st appellant Trust has to be governed by its bye-laws and hence I do not find anything wrong with the view taken by the trial court.
The appeal fails and is dismissed.
